subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following maintains the shape of the eyeball?
A Cornea
B Lens
C Vitreous humour
D Retina
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
The vitreous humour is the jelly-like fluid that fills the eyeball and keeps it firm, maintaining its shape. The cornea and lens refract light, and the retina contains photoreceptors.

subQuestions.questionText:
The choroid …
A is richly supplied with blood vessels.
B contains photoreceptors.
C refracts the light rays.
D sends impulses to the brain.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
The choroid is the middle, vascular layer of the eye; it is richly supplied with blood vessels that nourish the eye and contains pigment that absorbs light to prevent internal reflection. Photoreceptors are in the retina.

options.A: is richly supplied with blood vessels.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following occurs immediately after fertilisation?
A The blastula, which is a hollow ball of cells, is formed by meiosis.
B The morula, which is a hollow ball of cells, is formed by meiosis.
C The blastula, which is a solid ball of cells, is formed by mitosis.
D The morula, which is a solid ball of cells, is formed by mitosis.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Immediately after fertilisation the zygote divides by mitosis to form the morula, a solid ball of cells. (The blastula, a hollow ball of cells, forms later, also by mitosis.)

options.A: The blastula, which is a hollow ball of cells, is formed by meiosis.
options.B: The morula, which is a hollow ball of cells, is formed by meiosis.
options.C: The blastula, which is a solid ball of cells, is formed by mitosis.
options.D: The morula, which is a solid ball of cells, is formed by mitosis.

subQuestions.questionText:
On a hot day …
A less blood flows to the surface of the skin.
B the sweat glands become inactive.
C more blood flows to the surface of the skin.
D vasoconstriction takes place.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
On a hot day vasodilation occurs, so more blood flows to the surface of the skin, allowing more heat to be lost to the environment. Vasoconstriction and inactive sweat glands occur on a cold day.

options.A: less blood flows to the surface of the skin.
options.C: more blood flows to the surface of the skin.

subQuestions.questionText:
The normal site of fertilisation in a human female is the …
A uterus.
B ovary.
C vagina.
D Fallopian tube.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Fertilisation normally takes place in the Fallopian tube (oviduct), where the sperm meets the released ovum after ovulation.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following best describes the events of accommodation when a person is viewing an object that is less than 6 m away?
Each option gives, in order: Ciliary muscle | Suspensory ligaments | Tension on the lens
A Relaxes | Tighten | Increases
B Contracts | Slacken | Decreases
C Relaxes | Slacken | Decreases
D Contracts | Tighten | Increases
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
When viewing a near object (less than 6 m away), the ciliary muscle contracts, the suspensory ligaments slacken and the tension on the lens decreases, so the lens becomes more rounded (thicker) to increase refraction.

options.A: Ciliary muscle relaxes; suspensory ligaments tighten; tension on the lens increases
options.B: Ciliary muscle contracts; suspensory ligaments slacken; tension on the lens decreases
options.C: Ciliary muscle relaxes; suspensory ligaments slacken; tension on the lens decreases
options.D: Ciliary muscle contracts; suspensory ligaments tighten; tension on the lens increases

subQuestions.questionText:
(Questions 1.1.9 and 1.1.10 refer to an investigation into the effect of auxins on tropism. A pot plant was placed on a stationary clinostat and exposed to light from all directions. After a few days the stem was observed growing upwards.)
Which ONE of the following is an explanation of the results?
A Phototropism occurred because the auxins moved towards light, which inhibited growth on the lower side of the stem.
B Geotropism occurred because the auxins moved downwards, which stimulated growth on the lower side of the stem.
C Phototropism occurred because the auxins moved away from light, which stimulated growth on the upper side of the stem.
D Geotropism occurred because the auxins moved upwards, which inhibited growth on the upper side of the stem.
(Refer to the clinostat diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Because the clinostat was stationary and light came from all directions, the response was to gravity (geotropism). Auxins moved downwards and stimulated more growth on the lower side of the horizontal stem, causing it to curve and grow upwards (negative geotropism).

options.A: Phototropism occurred because the auxins moved towards light, which inhibited growth on the lower side of the stem.
options.B: Geotropism occurred because the auxins moved downwards, which stimulated growth on the lower side of the stem.
options.C: Phototropism occurred because the auxins moved away from light, which stimulated growth on the upper side of the stem.
options.D: Geotropism occurred because the auxins moved upwards, which inhibited growth on the upper side of the stem.

subQuestions.questionText:
A control for the same investigation was set up by putting an identical pot plant on a rotating clinostat.
Which ONE of the following would be the expected results observed after a few days?
A There will be no growth.
B The stem will grow upwards.
C The stem will grow downwards.
D The stem will grow horizontally.
(Refer to the clinostat diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
On a rotating clinostat, gravity acts equally on all sides of the stem so no single side receives more auxin. There is no directional stimulus, so the stem continues to grow horizontally (in its original direction).

Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Column I: A plant hormone that inhibits the germination of seeds.
Column II — A: Gibberellins; B: Abscisic acid
subQuestions.memoText:
B only (2 marks)
Abscisic acid inhibits seed germination (promotes dormancy). Gibberellins do the opposite — they stimulate germination.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Column I: The functional connection between two consecutive neurons.
Column II — A: Synapse; B: Effector
subQuestions.memoText:
A only (2 marks)
The synapse is the functional connection (gap) between two consecutive neurons. An effector is a muscle or gland that responds to an impulse.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description in COLUMN I applies to A only, B only, both A and B, or none of the items in COLUMN II.
Column I: A hormone that stimulates puberty.
Column II — A: Testosterone; B: Oestrogen
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B (2 marks)
Testosterone stimulates puberty in males and oestrogen stimulates puberty in females, so both hormones stimulate puberty.

subQuestions.questionText:
Scientists investigated the effect of wearing face masks on the carbon dioxide levels in blood. They obtained permission from 150 healthy volunteers, aged 30, applied a sensor to the participants' skin to measure the carbon dioxide levels in the blood, and asked the participants to: sit still for 10 minutes without a face mask; sit still for 10 minutes wearing a face mask; exercise for 10 minutes without a face mask; and exercise for 10 minutes wearing a face mask. A 15-minute interval was allowed between each 10-minute phase, and the carbon dioxide levels were recorded at the end of each phase. The face mask covered the nose and mouth.
Identify the:
(a) Independent variable
(b) Dependent variable
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Wearing of a face mask (1 mark)
(b) Carbon dioxide levels in blood (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors that were taken into consideration in the selection of the participants.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (2 marks). Mark first TWO only:
- Age
- Healthy individuals

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the results at the end of this investigation may be considered reliable.
subQuestions.memoText: 150 volunteers were used (1 mark) (Mark first ONE only)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why scientists allowed a 15-minute interval between each phase.
subQuestions.memoText:
(2 marks)
Mark 1: To allow the carbon dioxide levels in the blood to go back to normal
Mark 2: so that each phase will have the same carbon dioxide level as a starting point

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason why the carbon dioxide levels were measured while participants were sitting still.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE of the following (1 mark):
- To act as a control / baseline
- To see if it is the face mask that affects the carbon dioxide levels and not the physical activity

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the homeostatic control of carbon dioxide when it is high in blood.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any SEVEN of the following (7 marks):
- Receptors in the carotid artery are stimulated and
- impulses are sent to the medulla oblongata
- The medulla oblongata stimulates the heart
- to beat faster, causing
- more carbon dioxide to be taken to the lungs
- The breathing muscles / intercostal muscles and diaphragm
- contract more actively and
- the rate / depth of breathing increases
- More carbon dioxide is exhaled
- The carbon dioxide level in the blood decreases / returns to normal
